decoys.summary: A later link reference definition replaces the destination and title of an earlier definition with the same case-insensitive label. For example, [ref]: /first followed by [REF]: /second makes [shown][ref] point to /second instead of preserving the first definition.
decoys.match_rule: The report must identify last-definition-wins behavior for duplicate ordinary link reference labels, including case-insensitive duplicates, and attribute the destination/title replacement to reference-definition insertion in the first pass.

refutation.evidence: Insertion uses entry(label).or_insert(link_def), which retains an occupied entry; LinkLabel is UniCase<CowStr>, and RefDefs::get also wraps its key in UniCase. The probe supplies [ref]: /first "first title" and then [REF]: /second "second title". Both the public reference-definition lookup and rendered full, collapsed, and shortcut references retain /first and first title. The later definition never overwrites either field. Probe source: /work/prepared/evidence/negative_controls.rs, test decoy_1_first_reference_definition_wins. Passing output: /work/prepared/evidence/decoy-1.log. Line references name the unchanged /work/crate baseline.
commands: cd /work/tmp/control-crate && cargo test --locked -p pulldown-cmark --test negative_controls decoy_1_first_reference_definition_wins -- --exact --nocapture

decoys.summary: Code-span edge-space normalization also removes the leading and trailing spaces when the entire payload consists of spaces. The two-space span `  ` therefore produces an empty Code event and empty <code> element instead of preserving both spaces.
decoys.match_rule: The report must identify loss of an all-space inline-code payload caused by make_code_span applying its surrounding-space trimming rule to that payload, such as turning a two-space code span into an empty one.

refutation.evidence: make_code_span computes all_spaces with s.bytes().all(|b| b == b' ') and requires !all_spaces as well as opening and closing spaces before trimming. An all-space payload falls through to preservation. The probe verifies exact Code-event payloads and exact HTML for spans containing 1, 2, 3, and 5 spaces: every space survives. It also verifies that ` a ` becomes a and `  a  ` becomes one-space/a/one-space, exercising the trimming branch on non-space content. Probe source: /work/prepared/evidence/negative_controls.rs, test decoy_2_all_space_code_spans_preserved. Passing output: /work/prepared/evidence/decoy-2.log. Line references name the unchanged /work/crate baseline.
commands: cd /work/tmp/control-crate && cargo test --locked -p pulldown-cmark --test negative_controls decoy_2_all_space_code_spans_preserved -- --exact --nocapture

false_findings.title: HTML I/O rendering silently truncates output on successful short writes
false_findings.body: Passing a conforming std::io::Write implementation that accepts only two bytes per write to html::write_html_io loses the unwritten suffixes of tags and text. The streaming rendering path treats each successful write as completion of the whole fragment instead of retrying the remaining bytes. Rendering an ordered list such as "3. café & tea" can therefore return Ok while producing incomplete HTML.

refutation.evidence: write_html_io wraps the supplied writer in IoWriter. Its StrWrite::write_str uses Write::write_all, and its formatted path delegates to Write::write_fmt, so short writes are retried by those I/O helpers. The probe uses an actual writer whose write accepts at most two bytes and records 25 calls, including 16 short writes. Rendering 3. café & tea returns Ok and exactly matches the full expected ordered-list HTML, including start="3", café, and &. Probe source: /work/prepared/evidence/negative_controls.rs, test false_1_io_short_writes_are_retried. Passing output: /work/prepared/evidence/false-1.log. Line references name the unchanged /work/crate baseline.
commands: cd /work/tmp/control-crate && cargo test --locked -p pulldown-cmark --test negative_controls false_1_io_short_writes_are_retried -- --exact --nocapture

false_findings.title: Nested inline end tags prematurely terminate image alt-text collection
false_findings.body: HtmlWriter::raw_text stops collecting an outer image description when it reaches the end of nested emphasis or a nested image. For ![before *em* ![inner](inner.png) after](outer.png) tail, this closes the outer alt attribute too early and renders the remaining description as ordinary page text. Image descriptions containing nested inline markup consequently lose their trailing alt text.

refutation.evidence:
The image start handler calls raw_text, whose nest counter increases on every nested Start and decreases on nested End. End terminates collection only when nest was already zero, so nested emphasis and image ends cannot close the outer description. The probe confirms that the parser emits two nested image starts and that rendering produces exactly

tail

followed by a newline. The full outer description stays in alt and the actual trailing text stays outside. Probe source: /work/prepared/evidence/negative_controls.rs, test false_2_nested_image_alt_keeps_outer_tail. Passing output: /work/prepared/evidence/false-2.log. Line references name the unchanged /work/crate baseline.
commands: cd /work/tmp/control-crate && cargo test --locked -p pulldown-cmark --test negative_controls false_2_nested_image_alt_keeps_outer_tail -- --exact --nocapture

false_findings.title: Table rows with missing trailing cells emit too few cells
false_findings.body: parse_table_row_inner returns a short body row after scanning only the cells physically present on its line, without adding the missing trailing cells required by the table header. With ENABLE_TABLES, a three-column table followed by the body row | one | emits one TableCell and renders only one td rather than three. Consumers that depend on a consistent column count receive ragged event rows and HTML.

refutation.evidence: The early return at line 519 is guarded by cells == 0, so it does not apply to a nonempty short row. Before returning a row, the subsequent for _ in cells..row_cells loop appends an empty TableCell for each missing column. The probe parses a three-column table with body rows containing one and two actual cells; both produce three TableCell starts. Exact HTML assertions confirm rows one and twothree. These are small ordinary rows within the completion guard. Probe source: /work/prepared/evidence/negative_controls.rs, test false_3_short_table_rows_are_padded. Passing output: /work/prepared/evidence/false-3.log. Line references name the unchanged /work/crate baseline.
commands: cd /work/tmp/control-crate && cargo test --locked -p pulldown-cmark --test negative_controls false_3_short_table_rows_are_padded -- --exact --nocapture

false_findings.title: Broken-link callback overrides references that already have definitions
false_findings.body: Parser::new_with_broken_link_callback invokes the supplied resolver even after finding an in-document reference definition. A callback that always supplies /fallback therefore replaces the destination and title of [ok][known] despite [known]: /defined "Defined" being present. Applications using a callback to fill missing links also rewrite links explicitly authored in the document.

refutation.evidence: fetch_link_type_url_title first resolves the reference through refdefs.get(...).map(...). The callback is inside Option::or_else, whose closure runs only when that lookup returned None. The probe installs an always-Some callback and parses a defined reference plus one missing reference. The callback receives only missing. The defined link retains LinkType::Reference, /defined, and Defined; the missing link receives ReferenceUnknown, /fallback, and Fallback. Exact rendered HTML preserves both results. Probe source: /work/prepared/evidence/negative_controls.rs, test false_4_defined_references_bypass_broken_link_callback. Passing output: /work/prepared/evidence/false-4.log. Line references name the unchanged /work/crate baseline.

false_findings.title: Repeated footnote references consume new display numbers
false_findings.body: The FootnoteReference rendering arm calculates the next number on every occurrence and assigns it even when the label has already been seen. With ENABLE_FOOTNOTES, first[^a] second[^a] third[^b] and definitions for a and b therefore display reference numbers 1, 2, 3 rather than 1, 1, 2. Repeating a reference changes the displayed identity of the same footnote and shifts numbering for later notes.

refutation.evidence: Although len is calculated on every occurrence, the displayed number comes from numbers.entry(name).or_insert(len). An occupied entry preserves its previous number and does not grow the map. The definition-rendering arm uses the same map and entry rule. The probe renders two references to a and one to b with both definitions, and asserts the entire HTML: reference numbers are exactly 1, 1, 2, while definition labels remain 1 and 2. Probe source: /work/prepared/evidence/negative_controls.rs, test false_5_repeated_footnotes_reuse_number. Passing output: /work/prepared/evidence/false-5.log. Line references name the unchanged /work/crate baseline.
commands: cd /work/tmp/control-crate && cargo test --locked -p pulldown-cmark --test negative_controls false_5_repeated_footnotes_reuse_number -- --exact --nocapture
